title: First-generation (sedating) antihistamines
drugs: brompheniramine; chlorphenamine; cyproheptadine; dimenhydrinate; diphenhydramine; doxylamine; hydroxyzine; meclozine; promethazine; triprolidine
advice: Avoid. A short course for a severe allergic reaction can still be appropriate.
reason: Strongly anticholinergic and cleared more slowly with age: confusion, dry mouth, constipation; long-term use is linked to falls, delirium and dementia.

title: Nitrofurantoin
advice: Applies to long-term use to prevent urine infections, or when kidney function is low (CrCl under 30).
reason: Can harm the lungs, liver and nerves with long use; safer options exist.

title: Aspirin for primary prevention
advice: Applies if aspirin is taken only to prevent a first heart attack or stroke: do not start it, and ask about stopping it. Aspirin after a heart attack or stroke is usually still right.
reason: Bleeding risk rises sharply with age, and for prevention alone the harm can outweigh the benefit.

title: Warfarin as a first choice
advice: Applies when starting a blood thinner for atrial fibrillation or a clot: newer ones (DOACs such as apixaban) are preferred. Long-term users with a stable INR may reasonably continue.
reason: More major bleeding, especially in the brain, than the newer blood thinners, and no better protection.

title: Rivaroxaban for long-term use
advice: Applies to long-term treatment of atrial fibrillation or clots: a safer blood thinner such as apixaban is usually preferred.
reason: Higher risk of major and stomach bleeding in older adults than other DOACs.

title: Dipyridamole (short-acting tablets)
advice: Avoid. Does not apply to the long-acting capsule combined with aspirin.
reason: Can drop blood pressure on standing; better options exist.

title: Doxazosin, prazosin, terazosin for blood pressure
advice: Applies when used for blood pressure; use for prostate symptoms is a separate decision.
reason: High risk of dizziness and falls from blood pressure dropping on standing.

title: Clonidine and similar for blood pressure
advice: Applies when used as a first-choice blood pressure medicine.
reason: Drowsiness and confusion, slow heartbeat, and dizziness on standing.

title: Nifedipine, immediate-release
advice: Applies to the quick-acting (immediate-release) form only; long-acting tablets are not included.
reason: Blood pressure can fall too fast and strain the heart.

title: Amiodarone as a first choice for atrial fibrillation
advice: Applies when it is the first medicine chosen for atrial fibrillation, unless there is heart failure or a thickened heart muscle.
reason: More side effects than other rhythm medicines.

title: Dronedarone
advice: Applies with permanent atrial fibrillation or severe or recently worsened heart failure.
reason: Worse outcomes in these patients.

title: Digoxin as a first choice
advice: Applies when it is the first medicine chosen for atrial fibrillation or heart failure; if used, keep the dose at or under 0.125 mg a day.
reason: Safer options exist, and it builds up when the kidneys slow with age.

title: Strongly anticholinergic antidepressants
drugs: amitriptyline; amoxapine; clomipramine; desipramine; doxepin; imipramine; nortriptyline; paroxetine
advice: Avoid. (Very low-dose doxepin, 6 mg a day or less, is an exception.)
reason: Strongly anticholinergic, sedating, and cause dizziness on standing.

title: Benzatropine, trihexyphenidyl
advice: Avoid, including for side effects of antipsychotics.
reason: Strongly anticholinergic; better treatments exist for Parkinson disease.

title: Antipsychotics
advice: Applies unless used for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or another approved reason. Avoid for behaviour problems in dementia or delirium unless other approaches have failed.
reason: Higher risk of stroke, faster memory decline and death in people with dementia.

title: Barbiturates
advice: Avoid.
reason: Easy to become dependent on, stop helping sleep, and risk of overdose even at low doses.

title: Benzodiazepines
advice: Avoid. May still be right for seizures, alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal, severe anxiety or before a procedure.
reason: Older adults are more sensitive: confusion, falls, fractures and road accidents; dependence and misuse; dangerous with opioids.

title: Z-drug sleeping tablets
advice: Avoid.
reason: Same harms as benzodiazepines (confusion, falls, fractures, hospital visits) for little extra sleep.

title: Meprobamate
advice: Avoid.
reason: Very sedating and easy to become dependent on.

title: Ergoloid mesylates
advice: Avoid.
reason: Does not work.

title: Testosterone
advice: Applies unless there is confirmed low testosterone with symptoms.
reason: Possible heart problems, and risk in men with prostate cancer.

title: Estrogen tablets or patches (HRT)
advice: Applies to tablets and patches: do not start them at this age, and ask about stopping. Low-dose vaginal creams or tablets are fine.
reason: Started at 60 or older, the risks (breast and womb cancer, heart disease, stroke, clots, dementia) outweigh the benefits.

title: Sulfonylureas for diabetes
advice: Applies when used as a first or second diabetes medicine while safer ones are available. If one is needed, a short-acting one (glipizide) is preferred over glimepiride or glibenclamide.
reason: More low sugar episodes, heart problems and deaths than other diabetes medicines.

title: Desiccated thyroid
advice: Avoid; use levothyroxine instead.
reason: Concerns about effects on the heart.

title: Megestrol
advice: Avoid.
reason: Adds little weight and raises the risk of clots and possibly death.

title: Growth hormone
advice: Applies unless there is a proven growth hormone deficiency.
reason: Small benefit with swelling, joint pain and raised blood sugar.

title: Stomach acid tablets (PPIs) for more than 8 weeks
advice: Applies when taken every day for more than 8 weeks without a clear reason (such as long-term steroids or painkillers, or severe reflux damage).
reason: Long-term use is linked to gut infections (C. difficile), pneumonia, bone loss and fractures.

title: Metoclopramide
advice: Avoid, except for gastroparesis for no more than 12 weeks.
reason: Can cause movement disorders, sometimes permanent (tardive dyskinesia).

title: Strongly anticholinergic stomach antispasmodics
advice: Avoid (atropine eye drops are not included).
reason: Strongly anticholinergic, and it is unclear that they help.

title: Liquid paraffin (mineral oil) by mouth
drugs: liquid paraffin; mineral oil; light mineral oil; white mineral oil
advice: Avoid; use another laxative.
reason: Can be breathed into the lungs by mistake.

title: Desmopressin for night-time urination
advice: Applies when used for passing urine at night.
reason: High risk of low sodium in the blood.

title: Painkillers of the NSAID type, long-term
advice: Applies to regular long-term use, or any regular use with steroids or blood thinners, unless nothing else works and a stomach-protecting tablet is taken too.
reason: Stomach ulcers and bleeding (more likely over 75), raised blood pressure and kidney damage.

title: Indomethacin and ketorolac
advice: Avoid.
reason: The highest risk of stomach bleeding and kidney injury of all NSAIDs; indomethacin also affects the brain.

title: Pethidine (meperidine)
advice: Avoid; safer painkillers exist.
reason: Works poorly by mouth and can cause confusion and other nerve toxicity.

title: Muscle relaxants
drugs: carisoprodol; chlorzoxazone; cyclobenzaprine; metaxalone; methocarbamol; orphenadrine
advice: Avoid. (Baclofen and tizanidine for spasticity are not included.)
reason: Poorly tolerated: anticholinergic effects, drowsiness and fractures, with doubtful benefit at safe doses.

title: Worsens heart failure
drugs: cilostazol; diltiazem; verapamil; dronedarone; pioglitazone; rosiglitazone; nabumetone; nimesulide
atc: M01AA; M01AB; M01AC; M01AE; M01AG; M01AH
advice: Avoid cilostazol; avoid diltiazem and verapamil if the heart pumps weakly; avoid NSAIDs, pioglitazone and dronedarone if heart failure causes symptoms.
reason: Can cause fluid build-up and make heart failure worse, or raise the risk of death.

title: Worsens fainting
drugs: chlorpromazine; olanzapine; donepezil; galantamine; rivastigmine; doxazosin; prazosin; terazosin; amitriptyline; clomipramine; doxepin; imipramine
advice: Avoid.
reason: Lower blood pressure on standing or slow the heartbeat, which can cause more fainting.

title: Worsens delirium (sudden confusion)
drugs: @table7; clonazepam; clobazam; cimetidine; famotidine; nizatidine; eszopiclone; zaleplon; zolpidem; codeine
atc: N05A; N05BA; N05CD; H02AB; A02BA; N05CF; N02A
advice: Avoid in anyone with, or at high risk of, delirium. Steroids, if needed, at the lowest dose for the shortest time.
reason: Can bring on or worsen sudden confusion.

title: Worsens dementia
advice: Avoid. Antipsychotics only when other approaches for behaviour problems have failed.
reason: Harm memory and thinking; antipsychotics also raise the risk of stroke and death in dementia.

title: Raises the risk of another fall
drugs: @table7; clonazepam; clobazam; venlafaxine; desvenlafaxine; duloxetine; milnacipran; levomilnacipran; gabapentin; pregabalin; eszopiclone; zaleplon; zolpidem; codeine
atc: N06AB; N06AA; N03; N05A; N05BA; N05CD; N05CF; N02A
advice: Avoid unless there is no safer option; antiepileptics only for seizures or mood disorders, opioids only for severe short-term pain. If one is needed, cut down the others on this list.
reason: Unsteadiness, slowed reactions and fainting lead to more falls and fractures.

title: Worsens Parkinson disease
exclude: clozapine; pimavanserin; quetiapine; lithium carbonate; lithium citrate
advice: Avoid. (Clozapine, pimavanserin and quetiapine are less likely to cause problems.)
reason: Block dopamine and can make Parkinson symptoms worse.

title: Worsens stomach ulcers
advice: Avoid unless nothing else works and a stomach-protecting tablet is taken too.
reason: Can worsen ulcers or cause new ones.

title: Worsens urine leakage in women
advice: Avoid in women (vaginal estrogen is not included).
reason: Alpha-blockers make leakage worse; estrogen tablets do not help it.

title: Worsens prostate or bladder emptying problems in men
exclude: darifenacin; fesoterodine; flavoxate; oxybutynin; solifenacin; tolterodine; trospium
advice: Avoid in men (bladder medicines for leakage are a separate decision).
reason: Weaken the urine flow and can stop urine altogether.

title: Dabigatran
advice: Other blood thinners (such as apixaban) are usually preferred for long-term use.
reason: More stomach and major bleeding than some alternatives.

title: Prasugrel, ticagrelor
advice: Use with care, especially from age 75; for prasugrel a lower dose (5 mg) is advised at 75 and over.
reason: More major bleeding than clopidogrel in older adults.

title: Can lower sodium in the blood
drugs: mirtazapine; carbamazepine; oxcarbazepine; tramadol; venlafaxine; desvenlafaxine; duloxetine; milnacipran; levomilnacipran
advice: Check the blood sodium level when starting or changing the dose.
reason: Can cause low sodium (SIADH), which brings confusion, falls and fits.

title: SGLT2 diabetes medicines (gliflozins)
advice: Watch for urine and genital infections, especially in the first month, and for ketoacidosis.
reason: Older adults are more prone to these infections and to ketoacidosis with normal sugar.

title: Two blood pressure medicines that raise potassium
advice: Avoid using two of these together routinely, especially with kidney disease (stage 3a or worse).
reason: Potassium in the blood can rise too high.

title: Opioid with a benzodiazepine
advice: Avoid.
reason: Higher risk of overdose and dangerous side effects.

title: Opioid with gabapentin or pregabalin
advice: Avoid, except while switching from one to the other or using them to lower the opioid dose.
reason: Severe drowsiness, slowed breathing and death.

title: Lithium with an ACE inhibitor or ARB
advice: Avoid; if used, check lithium blood levels.
reason: Lithium can build up to toxic levels.

title: Lithium with a loop diuretic
advice: Avoid; if used, check lithium blood levels.
reason: Lithium can build up to toxic levels.

title: Doxazosin/prazosin/terazosin with a loop diuretic
advice: Applies to older women, unless both are really needed.
reason: More urine leakage.

title: Phenytoin with co-trimoxazole
advice: Avoid.
reason: Phenytoin can build up to toxic levels.

title: Theophylline with cimetidine or ciprofloxacin
advice: Avoid.
reason: Theophylline can build up to toxic levels.

title: Warfarin with a medicine that raises bleeding risk
advice: Avoid when possible; if both are needed, check the INR closely.
reason: More bleeding.

title: Two or more anticholinergic medicines
advice: Avoid; keep the number of anticholinergic medicines as low as possible.
reason: Together they raise the risk of memory decline, delirium, falls and fractures.

title: Three or more medicines acting on the brain
drugs: clonazepam; clobazam; venlafaxine; desvenlafaxine; duloxetine; milnacipran; levomilnacipran; gabapentin; pregabalin; eszopiclone; zaleplon; zolpidem; codeine
atc: N03; N06AA; N06AB; N05A; N05BA; N05CD; N05CF; N02A; N07BC; M03B
advice: Avoid taking three or more together; keep the number as low as possible.
reason: More falls and fractures.

title: Strongly anticholinergic medicines
drugs: amitriptyline; amoxapine; clomipramine; desipramine; doxepin; imipramine; nortriptyline; paroxetine; prochlorperazine; promethazine; brompheniramine; chlorphenamine; cyproheptadine; dimenhydrinate; diphenhydramine; doxylamine; hydroxyzine; meclozine; triprolidine; darifenacin; fesoterodine; flavoxate; oxybutynin; solifenacin; tolterodine; trospium; benzatropine; trihexyphenidyl; chlorpromazine; clozapine; olanzapine; perphenazine; atropine; clidinium; dicycloverine; homatropine; hyoscyamine; scopolamine; cyclobenzaprine; orphenadrine
